title: A letter from Nairobi
text:
14 Jacaranda Road
Nairobi
Kenya
12 March

Dear Putri,

Thank you for your lovely postcard of the Prambanan temples. I stuck it on the wall next to my bed, and my little brother Kamau says it is the best picture in our house. I do not agree. I think the photograph of our dog is better!

Your letter made me laugh when you described the rainy season. In Nairobi we have two rainy seasons each year: the long rains from March to May and the short rains later in the year. It is March now, so the rain has only just started. The garden smells wonderful, and the frogs sing every night.

At school, we have started a new project. Every Friday, Class 4 reads to the younger children for twenty minutes. I have been paired with a girl called Zawadi, who is six. She reads slowly and points to each word with her finger. Last Friday she read a whole page without any help, and she was so happy that she hugged me. I think reading buddies is the best idea our teacher has ever had.

Do you have anything like that at your school? Please write and tell me. I would also like to know what you eat for breakfast. Here, most children have porridge or bread and tea. Mum says breakfast is the most important meal of the day, but I am not sure that is true on a Saturday, when I can have pancakes at ten o'clock.

Write soon!

Your friend,
Amara
